summary: Intermittent inference hangs and upstream reset for long completions caused by oversized trace/cookie headers and ALB proxy buffering
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent high tail latency and occasional 502/504 errors for long-running generation requests (responses > 10s) originating from their dedicated pool. Problem appears correlated with requests containing very large tracing headers (X-Trace-Path) and multiple large cookie headers set by the customer app.

Impact:
- Several live sessions experience stalled streaming and final 502/504s.
- Affected LumenVoice production traffic only (dedicated capacity).
- Increased P50->P99 latency for generation calls during affected windows; customer reports user-visible audio generation delays.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated for LumenVoice (dedicated pool: lv-dedicated-03) in us-east-1.
- API fronted by ALB + internal API gateway with proxy buffering enabled.
- Serving runtime version: 2026.02.11-release

Steps to reproduce (observed patterns):
1) Customer issues a long completion request with streaming (chunked) enabled and heavy trace headers (X-Trace-Path ~ 48KB) plus several cookies totaling ~12KB.
2) Request initially accepted by API gateway; request sits in proxy buffer longer than typical as the runtime is performing large KV cache warmup for cold sequence.
3) ALB or gateway completes internal buffer/timeout behavior then tears down connection (reset) leading to client-observed 502/504 or streaming stalls.

Observed behavior:
- Connection resets seen in ALB logs: Target response time spikes, followed by 502/504 and TCP RST on the target connection.
- NLB/ALB access logs show truncated header warnings for a subset of requests.
- Serving runtime shows completed token counts but missing final flush to client in some traces.

Expected behavior:
- Long completions should stream progressively without ALB/gateway-induced resets even when headers are large, or the platform should return a clearer 413-like error when headers exceed limits instead of silent resets.

Logs & telemetry:
- ALB access logs (S3): s3://redwood-logs/alb/2026/03/12/ALB-lv-dedicated-03.log (examples attached in ticket).
- Gateway error traces: trace IDs start with lv-3a8f.
- Serving runtime traces: trace-20260312-3a8f-01 (KV warmup latency spikes).
- CloudWatch metrics: backend_target_5xx_count and backend_latency_p99 increased between 2026-03-12T13:15Z and 2026-03-12T14:05Z.

Initial triage notes:
- SRE observed correlation between large request header sizes and proxy buffering causing head-of-line blocking at the API gateway.
- Hypothesis A: ALB/gateway proxy buffers the full request headers and/or initial request body, and when buffers fill the connection is reset or idle-timed out.
- Hypothesis B: Serving runtime KV cache warmup increases server-side time-to-first-byte (TTFB) beyond ALB idle thresholds when combined with upstream buffering, exposing idle timeout behavior.
- Reproduced in staging by replaying customer's headers and increasing artificial KV warmup delay. Staging triggered same ALB truncated header log entries and resets.

Workaround (customer-facing):
- Reduce trace header size and consolidate cookies where possible (short-term).
- Disable verbose tracing for sessions expected to perform long completions.
- If using the SDK, enable smaller chunk sizes and set keepalive to true to reduce perceived idle timeouts.

Next steps / action items:
- SRE: Adjust ALB timeout thresholds and maximum header size temporarily for lv-dedicated-03 to prevent resets (owner: Daniel Kim).
- Platform: Investigate moving to streaming-first proxy behavior that forwards initial bytes immediately instead of waiting for full buffer (owner: Priya Desai).
- Runtime: Add a server-side early reject with clear 431/413 when header sizes exceed safe limits (owner: Marco Alvarez).
- Customer success: Advise LumenVoice engineering on header reduction patterns and assist with staged rollout of gateway config changes (owner: Rebecca Li).

Acceptance criteria:
- No user-visible resets for repeated reproduction cases with headers similar to customer's; confirmed for 4 hours of traffic in us-east-1.
- Clear 431 error returned when customer sends headers exceeding hard platform limits instead of internal 502/504.

References:
- Slack: #support-lumenvoice thread (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C03ABC123)
- ALB runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/ALB+buffering+runbook
comments: 2026-03-12 13:40 UTC - Sofia Patel (Support): Opened after customer reported multiple user sessions with stalled streaming and 504s. Collected ALB logs and asked for full request sample headers.

2026-03-12 14:05 UTC - Daniel Kim (SRE): Confirmed truncated header warnings in ALB logs. Reproduced in staging by replaying headers; observed ALB reset when combined with simulated KV warmup delay. Tentatively rolling a temporary ALB max header size bump for lv-dedicated-03.

2026-03-12 15:20 UTC - Priya Desai (Platform): Noted gateway uses proxy buffering mode that waits for full header/body in certain routing rules. Will prototype a streaming-forward path to remove head-of-line buffer for long-running completions.

2026-03-12 16:00 UTC - LumenVoice (Customer): Provided sample request IDs and agreed to trim verbose tracing for the next 24 hours while Redwood applies mitigation. Asked for guidance to detect large headers on their side.

2026-03-13 09:30 UTC - Daniel Kim (SRE): ALB header limit increased temporarily, observed reduced 502/504 events in target logs during two 1-hour test windows. Follow-up: schedule platform change to avoid dependency on header limit increases.

2026-03-13 11:10 UTC - Marco Alvarez (Runtime): Added task to issue tracker to return 431 when header parsing exceeds safe buffer; PR referenced in this ticket (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/945).
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporary ALB header limits increased and customer advised to trim trace headers. Platform and runtime changes are in progress (see linked PRs).
